about.title: Who I am
paragraphs: I’m Aindrila Das — a Business Process Trainer at Accenture and a community builder who believes education and dignity should reach every child.
Alongside professional work, I’ve volunteered with NGOs focused on libraries, donations, and fundraising for underprivileged children — including COVID-19 book and relief campaigns.

This page showcases that contribution honestly: clear about my volunteer role, concrete about published organizational reach, framed carefully so organizational reach stays distinct from personal contribution.

contributions.title: My contributions
contributions.intro: Three ways I’ve shown up — in my own voice, with organizational context for scale, without inventing personal KPIs or rupee totals.

cards.title: Libraries
cards.body: I helped set up and support libraries so children in underserved communities could access books and a quiet place to learn. That work sat inside a broader movement: Prashraya (Team Aashraya) publicly cites 400+ free libraries nationwide — scaled with district partnerships in places like Narsinghpur and Moradabad — plus learning centres and Aashraya Vidyalayas.
cards.note: My role: volunteer/contributor supporting library efforts — not a personal library-count KPI.

cards.title: Donation drives
cards.body: I organized and took part in donation efforts — collecting and coordinating books, essentials, and relief materials. Context for the drives I joined: Aashraya/Prashraya’s COVID-19 nationwide book collection (~1,00,000 books with ~1,500 volunteers joining quickly), and Hamari Pahchan’s published 1,500+ COVID-19 kits.
cards.note: My role: participant in drives — org kit/book totals are theirs, not personal tallies.

cards.title: Fundraising campaigns
cards.body: I hosted and supported fundraising campaigns for underprivileged children — including COVID-19 campaigns tied to book drives and relief kits — bringing people together and helping channel support toward education and welfare.

campaigns.title: Campaigns & timeline
campaigns.intro: Key org-documented moments that frame the volunteer work I took part in.

items.title: Hamari Pahchan founded (Delhi)
items.body: Founded by Tarun Mathur. Programs include Drishti (education), Sukhad (menstrual health), skill development, and later COVID response (corona kits + Gadgetshala). Published impact: 2,25,000+ children, 80,000+ women.

items.title: Team Aashraya → Prashraya Welfare Foundation
items.body: Founded 2019 in Tumda, Madhya Pradesh, by Priyanshu Khemariya as Team Aashraya; evolved into Prashraya. Focus: Shiksha, Shakti, Paryavaran, Chikitsa, Vastra. Public claims include 400+ free libraries, 35 learning centres, 9 Aashraya Vidyalayas (+ digital centre), 10,000+ volunteers, and 20+ states reach.

items.title: Nationwide book collection (Aashraya / Prashraya)
items.body: Indian Masterminds (Oct 2021) reported ~1,00,000 books collected in days, with ~1,500 volunteers joining quickly; the drive expanded pan-India across ~25 states/UTs for rural libraries, schools, and orphanages. The team also contributed actively during COVID-19 across Shiksha, Chikitsa, and related pillars.

items.title: COVID relief kits (Hamari Pahchan)
items.body: Hamari Pahchan’s public resources cite 1,500+ COVID-19 kits distributed, alongside broader resource programs (including menstrual kits framed at 50,000+ on the resources page).

items.title: Library expansion & education access
items.body: Continued growth of free libraries and learning centres — including partnerships with district administrations (e.g. Narsinghpur & Moradabad). About-page language also cites 800+ libraries established/supported via district partnerships; this showcase prefers the primary 400+ free libraries figure from projects.

panels.name: Prashraya Welfare Foundation
panels.body: A youth-led Section 8 non-profit that began in 2019 as Team Aashraya in Tumda, Madhya Pradesh, and evolved into Prashraya Welfare Foundation. Focus areas: Shiksha, Shakti, Paryavaran, Chikitsa, and Vastra. Founded by Priyanshu Khemariya.
stats: 400+ free libraries (primary; about also cites 800+ via partnerships)
~1,00,000 books in COVID-19 nationwide drive · ~1,500 volunteers joined quickly
panels.note: Organizational claims from public materials — not personal metrics.

panels.name: Hamari Pahchan NGO
panels.body: A Delhi-based NGO working across education, skill development, hunger relief, menstrual health, and community programs. Flagship initiatives include Drishti (education), Sukhad (menstrual), skill development, and COVID response (corona kits + Gadgetshala).
panels.note: Organizational claims from public materials — not personal metrics.

connection.title: How this work connects
paragraphs: Libraries without books, or children without the means to stay in school, leave gaps that no single classroom can fill. My volunteer work — supporting libraries inside a 400+ free-library movement, organizing donations and COVID-19 drives, and hosting fundraising campaigns — was aimed at one thread: education access for underprivileged children.

Each activity feeds the next: spaces to learn, materials to fill them, and community support to keep those efforts alive. That’s the impact story I can own honestly — contribution alongside published org reach, not inflated certificates.
